label: Toast
title: Toast
summary: Use a Toast to confirm something that just happened, such as a payment or a copy, in a short message that closes itself.
corePrinciple: Confirm, briefly, then get out of the way.

anatomy.title: A dark pill with a message
anatomy.description: A toast is a dark pill holding one message and, if you ask for it, a leading icon. It has no buttons; it closes itself.
blocks: Dark grey with 14 px corners and a soft shadow; the same in every mode.
Optional 18 px icon; the card icon unless you swap it.
White 14 px text, up to two lines.

configuration.title: Message, icon, and brand
configuration.description: A toast is one message with an optional leading icon. Only the icon follows AppearanceBrand; the pill is the same dark grey in every mode. Where toasts appear, top or bottom, is set once on the screen's provider: try it in the playground.
blocks: The default: one line of white text in a dark pill.
startItem adds the card icon before the message, white by default, as in Figma.
Swap in another 18 px icon; it takes the Coin icon colour, a deeper gold.
AppearanceBrand recolours only the icon: gold, purple, blue, or white, the default.

states.title: Shown, stacked, and gone
states.description: A toast slides in from its edge and closes itself after 4 s, or after its own timeout; with no timeout it stays until the screen clears it. Up to three show at once, newest last. Older ones wait behind them on their own timers, so they appear only if they’re still due when a newer one closes. There's no close button and no swipe.
blocks: Five at once: the newest three show; the first two time out behind them and never appear.

examples.description: Five at once: the newest three show; the first two time out behind them and never appear.

sizing.title: Hugs its message, within 90% of the screen
sizing.description: A toast is as wide as its message, at least 200 px and at most 90% of its screen, with 16 px of padding at the sides and 14 px above and below. Long messages wrap to two lines, then end in an ellipsis, unless the toast is added with disableTruncation, which shows every line.
blocks: Even one word gets a 200 px pill.
It wraps to two lines, then ends in an ellipsis; the rest is lost.

content.title: One short sentence about what happened
content.description: Say what happened in a few words, such as Payment successful or UPI ID copied. A toast has no buttons and closes itself, so never ask for a decision or put anything in it that people must read twice.
blocks: Short, specific, and about something that already happened.

sources.title: Use the public Toast contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (16 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Toast is one 291 × 46 component with a text, an optional start icon, and an icon swap; its icon resolves to white. Since the #267 fix the default icon is white too; an AppearanceBrand mode recolours it, while the pill stays the same dark grey in every mode. Screens add toasts with addToast and show them through one ToastProvider: every provider shows the same queue, so this page mounts one at a time. Toasts slide in from their edge and fade out, as in the package, and messages stop at two lines unless addToast sets disableTruncation. Each toast is announced as an alert. The published Storybook page is still the old generated one.
